episodes.183753: A diffuse dryline mixed into the Rolling Plains on the afternoon of the 19th. Hot temperatures east of the dryline led to a deeply mixed boundary layer eroding a cap that was in place. Strong instability and moderate deep layer shear contributed to strong supercell development from the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle into the northern Rolling Plains. One of these storms became severe in eastern Childress County producing hail up to baseball size.
episodes.183835: Residual moisture paired with orographic support and daytime heating led to scattered showers and thunderstorms over the San Juan Mountains. Some of the stronger storms in northern La Plata County produced strong winds that damaged cottonwood trees and some windows.
episodes.184775: Sufficient moisture and lift resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced strong wind gusts and damage.
episodes.185075: A thunderstorm produced a strong wind gust along the Indian River County coastline near Sebastian.
episodes.185534: As multiple low-amplitude upper waves (embedded within broad zonal flow) traversed the Southern Plains, two rounds of convection occurred across the forecast area on the 19th. The first round, from the late morning into early afternoon, included a few reports of marginally severe hail across north-central into eastern Oklahoma, owing to relatively weak instability present during this time frame. ||By the early evening, aided by sufficient deep-layer wind shear and increasing (significant in magnitude) convective instability, multiple supercell thunderstorms initiated across southwest Oklahoma. Reports of large to very large hail and wind damage were received across the aforementioned areas. A 'left-split' (supercell) thunderstorm traveled into portions of central Oklahoma, including the southern suburbs of the Oklahoma City Metropolitan area, and produced continued reports of significant hail during the late evening time frame. Additional supercell thunderstorms developed further north across central Oklahoma during the evening as well. While a few reports of large hail were also received with these storms, greater convective inhibition limited the longevity of impact from these thunderstorms.
episodes.185535: During the early evening of the 19th, aided by sufficient deep-layer wind shear and increasing (significant in magnitude) convective instability, multiple supercell thunderstorms initiated off of a dryline across western-north Texas. Reports of large to very large hail and wind damage were received across the area.
episodes.185589: A small cluster of showers and thunderstorms developed over eastern New Mexico on the evening of the 18th and moved into the eastern TX Panhandle. Conditions favored some strong wind gusts from storms, and these storms did produce a gust of 59 mph measured by a mesonet station in Oldham County.
episodes.185763: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed with the passage of a warm front pushing across Iowa with a weakening low level jet. These storms produced some sub-severe hail and heavy rain.
episodes.185787: Scattered thunderstorms developed over portions of Northwest Kansas. These storms mainly moved over Decatur, Sheridan, Norton, and Graham counties. These storms produced pea to quarter sized hail in Decatur and Sheridan counties, with the largest hail falling near Hoxie, Kansas.
episodes.185834: Thunderstorms produced hail and winds across western Kansas.  A landspout was also reported.
episodes.185890: Elevated instability up to 1000 J/kg with a pulse of warm advection ahead of a weak mid-level wave resulted in scattered nocturnal storms, with the strongest producing marginally large hail.
episodes.185944: A frontal boundary situated over Central Florida brought a warm and moist airmass over South Florida, which combined with ample lift from mid-level troughing to develop scattered showers and thunderstorms over the area during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.185945: A frontal boundary situated over Central Florida brought a warm and moist airmass over South Florida, which combined with ample lift from mid-level troughing to develop scattered showers and thunderstorms over the area during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.186117: An upper-level trough was positioned over the central Gulf of Mexico, with a stationary surface front over central Florida.  Moist, northeast lower tropospheric flow allowed for the development of scattered thunderstorms over the eastern Straits of Florida, with isolated gale-force outflow wind gusts resulting.
episodes.186118: A waterspout was observed in association with isolated convective showers developing south of a stationary front.
episodes.186140: The region had a glancing blow from Hurricane Lee which passed into the Canadian Maritime on the 16th, bringing strong winds but limited rainfall to the local area. The more notable rainfall came a few days later when a low pressure system moved from Cape Cod into coastal Maine on the 18th into the 19th. This storm system brought a soaking rain of 1 to 3 inches to the region, with highest amounts near the coast. The reported impacts were in the mountainous region with minor road flooding.
episodes.186141: On September 19th, a robust storm produced some hail and damaging winds in Denton County, moving into Dallas County. Later that evening, a cluster of storms developed to our west and northwest, producing some hail and damaging winds in our western counties. On September 21st, another cluster of storms skirted along the Red River producing large hail in Denton County and flash flooding in Grayson County.
episodes.189226: A highly visible landspout tornado moved slowly northwest from 552 to 558 pm. Numerous pictures of this event were shared on social media. This landspout flipped a section of center pivot just south of Highway 96.
